text.p: DSM NV said on Tuesday it was adapting its dividend policy to produce a more stable and predictable payout to ordinary shareholders.

"Our dividend will henceforth be determined as a percentage of cashflow from ordinary activities after deduction of the dividend payable to holders of cumulative preference shares," DSM chairman Simon de Bree said in the 1996 annual report.
"This percentage will lie within a range of 16 to 20 percent. Since depreciation forms a relatively fixed component of cashflow, this means a more stable and easier to predict dividend," he added.
De Bree further added that DSM would start offering stock dividends as a structural element of dividend policy.
In view of the company's strong balance sheet with a high shareholders' equity, the company had also decided to buy back shares to at least the value of the stock dividend paid out.

DSM said that ever since it gained a stock exchange listing in 1989, its dividend policy had been aimed at a pay-out which reflected earnings fluctuations only to a limited degree, but that nevertheless past pay-outs had fluctuated widely.
